name: Watch to Grow
manifesto: Pick a need, not a genre. Every film is a learning card: what they may learn, what to ask, and what to try after the credits.

needs.name: Curiosity
needs.parent: I want my child to become more curious.
needs.promise: The child leaves with a question they did not have before. Wonder is the point.

needs.name: World Knowledge
needs.parent: I want them to understand the world.
needs.promise: A real place, era, culture, or civic fact becomes discussable — a doorway, not a lecture.

needs.name: Resilience
needs.parent: I want them to become more resilient.
needs.promise: A character stays with a hard thing. Afterward you can name the skill, not just the plot.

needs.name: Creativity
needs.parent: I want them to think creatively.
needs.promise: Making, inventing, or seeing differently is the engine of the story — not decoration.

needs.name: Empathy
needs.parent: I want them to understand other people.
needs.promise: The child practices standing in someone else's shoes, including people who are hard to like.

needs.name: STEM
needs.parent: I want them to become interested in STEM.
needs.promise: Science, technology, engineering, or math drives the plot. Not a chalkboard cameo.

needs.name: Learn Through Stories
needs.parent: I want something educational but fun.
needs.promise: Fun first. Learning sneaks in. Use when tonight should not feel like homework.

ages.blurb: Shorter nights, gentler stakes, play after the credits.
Feelings, fairness, and first hard questions.
History, science, and social pressure with room to talk.
Heavier themes. Preview first. Still a conversation, not a lecture.

howTo.headline: The parent is the user. The child is the learner. The film is the material.
howTo.lede: Watch to Grow is a lesson layer on top of movies you can already press play on. It is not a ranking of “best family films.”
howTo.note: If a card does not feel useful at your table, the page failed — not the child.

blocks.title: What a movie page contains
blocks.body: Recommended age, what kids may learn, qualities the story exercises, world knowledge, three conversation questions, one short activity, a parent note, and content notes worth previewing.

blocks.title: What not to do
blocks.body: Do not turn the questions into a test. Do not skip the content notes because the rating looks mild. Do not hunt only for the “educational” scene — the learning is usually in how a character decides.

blocks.title: What Phase 1 is not
blocks.body: No accounts. No watchlists. No star ratings. No “three films for my 11-year-old who loves science.” That is later, and only if these cards earn it.

ritual: Age is a parent call. Content notes are honest.
The film is the material. You are the teacher.
Do not quiz. If they shrug, offer your answer and stop.
Keep it under 30 minutes, while the story is still warm.
